messages:
kevin_support: Heads-up — Merchantly reports embedding drift vs last week on Dedicated (model: redwood-embed-v1). Similarity scores on their eval set dropped ~0.18 -> 0.12, breaking search ranking.

maria_pm: Thanks. How severe / revenue impact? Are they on reserved capacity?

tom_sales: Merchantly is on a Dedicated monthly commit. They marked it P1 — search is a core revenue path.

james_eng: Can you paste sample request IDs or the timeframe? Could be a routing fallback or quantization change.

kevin_support: Sample req ids: rq_8971, rq_8993. Issue noticed after Thu 03:40 UTC kernel/infra change.

sasha_se: I pulled the pool logs. We see routing fallbacks to embed-v1-quant for some shards when memory pressure spikes. Fallback logic kicked in. :grimacing:

eva_sre: We had a memory pressure spike on merchantly-pool during that window. Autoscaler lagged and a few nodes hit OOM thresholds.

maria_pm: Options: quick hotfix to prevent fallback (targeted change) vs waiting for the next minor release with autoscale and buffer improvements. Tradeoffs?

james_eng: Hotfix is small: pin routing for merchantly-pool to prefer exact model, disable quant fallback for their pool. We can canary it at 5%. Need tests + rollout plan.

sasha_se: Canary plan proposal: 1) change routing policy for merchantly-pool 2) run 10k synthetic embeddings from their eval set 3) monitor similarity delta, latency, errors. Ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m holds.

deploy-bot: Deploy requested: routing-service v2.14.3 -> canary (5%). Triggered by @james_eng. CI: 12/12 green.

kevin_support: Customer comms? I suggest: say root cause = routing fallback to quantized variant after kernel upgrade; targeted canary fix in 2h, full rollout in 4–6h. Agree?

tom_sales: They need reassurance this won't lose data and an ETA. They're OK with the plan if comms are proactive.

maria_pm: Launch criteria for hotfix: canary shows similarity improvement >= +0.05 vs baseline AND no CPU/memory regressions. If canary fails, rollback and escalate.

eva_sre: I'll spin up a runbook and dashboards: embed-similarity, embed-latency, node-memory, qcache-hit. Alerts: similarity drop >0.02 vs baseline OR error rate >0.5%.

james_eng: Opening PR with change + test harness. PR: http://git/ru/pr/1234. Includes unit tests and simple integration harness.

sasha_se: Test note: ensure acceptance harness exercises both float and quant variants so we can prove routing doesn't hit quant.

kevin_support: Draft comms to customer: "We found routing fallback to a quantized variant after a kernel upgrade. We're deploying a targeted fix to ensure your requests use the verified model variant. We'll update within 6 hours and share post-fix metrics." Any edits?

tom_sales: Add apology + offer a follow-up one-on-one and postmortem. Also promise interim metrics.

maria_pm: Action items: @james_eng -> PR & kick canary; @eva_sre -> runbook + alerts; @sasha_se -> run synthetic tests; @kevin_support -> send customer comm at canary start; @tom_sales -> notify AM. I'll track progress.

kevin_support: :thumbsup: Starting now. Will post smoke results.

james_eng: Canary 5% started at 1795013000. Synthetic eval (10k queries): similarity mean +0.06 vs baseline, p95 latency +12ms. No memory spikes in canary nodes.

eva_sre: Monitoring green for initial 30m window. CPU and memory stable under thresholds.

deploy-bot: Canary ramped to 25% at 1795013400 by @deploy-bot.

sasha_se: 25% lever test run OK. Similarity uplift consistent. Ramping to 100% on next window if no regressions.

deploy-bot: Ramped to 100% at 1795013600. No rollback triggered.

kevin_support: Notified Merchantly at 1795013670 with the canary summary. Customer replied :relieved: "thanks, please share final numbers."

maria_pm: Marking incident P0 -> resolved for now. We'll include the fix in the next minor release notes and follow up with a postmortem. Longer-term: increase autoscale headroom and tweak fallback policy.

tom_sales: Merchantly requested an SLA credit; routing to finance/legal separately. Flagging as a follow-up.

kevin_support: Closing loop here. Will attach logs and postmortem draft in a follow-up thread.

maria_pm: Great. Thanks team — concise and practical run.
